definition: come or bring together for a meeting
memoryTip: Con-vene: come together for a meeting.
correctPassage: The board will convene next Monday to vote on the proposal.
wrongPassages: Managers announced they would convene the staff by sending everyone home early.
She tried to convene the jury by dismissing half the panel before opening statements.
Please convene the window before you leave so the rain does not get in.

definition: so lacking in originality as to be boring
memoryTip: So common it bans all interest — boringly ordinary.
correctPassage: What might have been a powerful speech was undermined by banal slogans.
wrongPassages: Critics praised the banal ending for inventing a structure no one had seen before.
Her banal theorem introduced an entirely new branch of mathematics overnight.
The lecture was banal: every claim was backed by rare archival finds and original proofs.

definition: not even or regular in pattern; unpredictable
memoryTip: Err + path: jumps around without a steady pattern.
correctPassage: Erratic attendance made it hard to keep the seminar on schedule.
wrongPassages: Astronomers call a star erratic when its brightness never changes across decades.
She kept an erratic schedule: the same three tasks at the same times each day.
His erratic explanation listed steps 1–5 with diagrams and a glossary for every term.

definition: not candid or sincere; falsely appearing frank
memoryTip: Dis + ingenuous (innocent) — fake sincerity, not genuine.
correctPassage: Claiming surprise at the outcome seemed disingenuous after months of warnings.
wrongPassages: Listeners found the lecture disingenuous because no term was left undefined on the board.
Her disingenuous apology named every harm and accepted full responsibility without excuses.
Judges called the ruling disingenuous because it carefully weighed both sides and cited law.

definition: waver between different opinions or actions
memoryTip: Vacillate like a vacuum of decision — swing back and forth.
correctPassage: Investors continue to vacillate between optimism and caution.
wrongPassages: They voted to vacillate: every hand went up on the first call with no discussion.
She tried to vacillate the injunction by serving an outdated address.
He tried to vacillate the drought narrative by renaming the emergency a dry spell.
